## Install

```bash
# needs bun ≥ 1.3 and imagemagick (logo build)
bun install
bun run build
cp dist/glint ~/.local/bin/
```

Single compiled binary. No Node, no Python, no runtime to babysit.

## Use

```bash
glint                      # interactive TUI (logo intro and all)
glint -p "fix the tests"   # headless one-shot

content.thinking: Alright, I've just finished a round of updates: I refined the TpsMeter usage, tweaked the auto-goal logic to avoid unnecessary classifier calls on small talk, and updated the prompt template to explicitly instruct the assistant to give brief, friendly replies to greetings without launching tools. I also ran the TypeScript type‑check (`bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`) and confirmed there were no compile errors, and I inspected the UI strings in `src/tui.tsx` to see what the status bar currently displays. The next logical step is to make the UI itself reflect the new behavior I just introduced. In the web interface (`site/index.html`), there’s a status line that shows a compact summary of the current configuration and mode, e.g.: ```html compound · effort high · ctx 6.4k · 38.7k tok · $0.00 · safe · diag on ``` Now that I’ve added a brief‑reply rule for greetings, it would be helpful to surface a hint to the user that they can type `/help` to see the available commands or get more information about the interface. Adding “· /help” to that status line will make the hint visible without cluttering the UI. I need to edit `site/index.html` to replace the old string with the new one that includes the “· /help” suffix. This is a simple find‑and‑replace operation; there’s only one occurrence of that exact snippet, so I’ll set `replace_all` to false to avoid unintended changes elsewhere. Proceeding with the edit now.
